subject.title: Feature: Inject context window % into system prompt runtime section

question: Should OpenClaw expose passive context-window usage in the system-prompt Runtime line, and what exact freshness and display contract should it use?
rationale: The source path is clear, but adding volatile per-turn prompt metadata changes prompt semantics and cache behavior, so automation should not choose percentage-only versus raw tokens, stale-snapshot omission, or model-switch behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve bounded Runtime context metadata
options.body: Add a small context field below the cache boundary, using only fresh or explicitly documented previous-turn usage and focused tests for stale, compaction, and model-switch cases.

options.title: Keep explicit inspection only
options.body: Leave context usage on /context, /status, session_status, and diagnostics surfaces, and close or update this issue once maintainers decide passive prompt metadata is not desired.

options.title: Defer to broader context UX
options.body: Keep this open as dependent on a broader context/compaction visibility design instead of landing a narrow Runtime-line primitive now.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded Runtime context metadata
recommendation.body: Add a small context field below the cache boundary, using only fresh or explicitly documented previous-turn usage and focused tests for stale, compaction, and model-switch cases.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest history match for the current Runtime prompt path and the likely owner for a prompt-contract decision.
